tieu_de: Why Would Anyone Live in Oymyakon? I Tried.
mo_ta_dong: Around five hundred people live in Oymyakon, in Russia's Sakha Republic, often called the coldest permanently inhabited place on Earth. January averages around −46°C (−51°F). So why would anyone choose to live there? Wob went to move in, and found the answer in water that wouldn't freeze.
Warm springs, reindeer herders, a weather station that made a village famous, a highway built by Gulag prisoners, a fish that can stand up on its own, and a surprisingly hot July.

Wob is a cartoon. The trip is imagined; the facts are real and sourced.

How this was made: the narration voice is AI text-to-speech, and the script and animation code were written with AI assistance. There are no AI-generated images; Wob, the props and the maps are drawn in code. Every claim was checked separately by two AI models (Claude and Gemini) against published sources. Anything they disagreed on, or that one of them couldn't confirm, was looked up a third time, then kept, reworded or cut.
